ND-2025-SB2404.aiSummary: The law gives $1.5 million to the information technology department to update state websites and digital content for accessibility rules under the federal Americans with Disabilities Act. It also gives $325,000 to the public service commission for federal lawsuit intervention work. If that money is not enough, the commission may use a loan option through June 30, 2027. It took effect when filed with the secretary of state.

It affects property owners, renters, disabled veterans, school districts, and state tax and investment rules.

ND-2025-HB1143.aiSummary: It was signed into law and gives $5 million from a state fund to the agriculture commissioner for a food distribution facility grant program. The money can pay for land, design, engineering, labor, equipment, and materials for a statewide charitable food distribution and logistics facility. Groups that get the money must match each state dollar with one dollar from nonstate sources and report each year on how the money was used.

ND-2025-SB2011.aiSummary: The bill was signed into law and gives money for the North Dakota Highway Patrol for the July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027 budget period. It sets funds for patrol costs, some one-time items like motor pool costs and equipment, and allows certain fund transfers. It also lets each patrol officer get up to $200 a month in added travel-related pay and carries over $45,000 for past tech work.
